rationale: Master switch for the entire AI layer. The tool must remain fully functional with this false — enforced by tests/governance/test_ai_disabled.py.
source: Design specification for the AI layer.

rationale: Each AI feature is INDEPENDENTLY switchable. No AI feature may set or change a disposition, priority or exposure under any setting.
source: Design specification for the AI layer.

rationale: Default LLM provider. OfflineDeterministicProvider requires no API key and no network, so the artefact is reproducible and demonstrable offline.
source: Design specification for the AI layer.

rationale: A runaway rule must not flood the queue (a platform requirement). A rule exceeding this ceiling is auto-routed to MONITOR_ONLY and raises a governance event.
source: Chosen for this artefact: 8% of a 5,000-claim run.

rationale: Reviewer capacity used to calibrate model thresholds to capacity rather than to a fixed significance level. Drives precision@capacity.
source: Chosen for this artefact. A real deployment would measure this.

rationale: CLN-01-R02. the design permits "median/MAD OR PERCENTILE-BASED robust statistics", and amount per inpatient day is a RATIO of two skewed quantities, so its tail is far heavier than either. A modified-z cut of 3.5 on this metric flags 699 of 5,000 claims (14%), which breaches the alert-volume ceiling and would be an unusable queue — the number is describing the tail of a ratio distribution, not a population of suspect claims. The percentile form is used instead: it is inside that menu, it is interpretable to a reviewer ("in the top 1% of comparable claims per day"), and it is volume-controlled by construction. The modified-z residual is still computed and shown on the signal.
source: The design permits percentile-based robust statistics; the percentile is chosen for this artefact.

rationale: PAY-06-R04, second limb: suspiciously INVARIANT approval (unusually low variance in the approval ratio) versus peers, which can indicate adjudication manipulation and links to PAY-11. Expressed as a percentile of the peer variance distribution for the same reason as the first limb.
source: the control catalogue wording; the percentile is chosen for this artefact.

rationale: PAY-06-R04, first limb. the control catalogue says "persistently low approval ratio... VERSUS PEERS", so the comparison is to the peer distribution, not to a fixed ratio. A provider whose shrunk approved-to-billed ratio falls below this percentile of the peer distribution is flagged for education or audit — never denial. On the claim extract the lowest shrunk provider ratio is 0.651 and the median 0.859, so a fixed cut at, say, 0.55 could never fire; the percentile adapts to whatever the peer distribution actually is.
source: the control catalogue wording ('versus peers'); the percentile is chosen for this artefact.

rationale: ENT-03-R02 / CLN-06-R02: an exclusion-list match may only REJECT on an EXACT identifier match. A fuzzy match may only PEND. the control catalogue states this explicitly and the rule contract encodes it.
Multiplier applied to declared capacity before a capacity breach is declared, absorbing roster and data-latency error (control catalogue, CLN-07-R02: 'missing roster produces low confidence').
CLN-01-R04. A provider-month enters the top-level-share series only with at least this many graded service lines, so a single month of three visits cannot swing the series.

CLN-01-R04. Minimum absolute rise in the share of graded services billed at the top level of their code family before a level-migration change point is reported; a smaller statistically clear shift is not material enough to audit.

CLN-02-R03. A diagnosis category counts as long-standing when at least this share of the patients who have it at all have it on more than one claim; learnt from the file rather than from a fixed code list.

CLN-02-R02 and CLN-05-R04. Tail probability of the observed count under the risk-adjusted expectation (Poisson or binomial) below which the excess is treated as more than chance; strict because every provider is tested.
CLN-02-R02. Minimum inpatient stays before a provider's complication-code rate is compared with risk-adjusted peers (catalogue exclusion: minimum volume).

CLN-02-R02. Observed-to-expected ratio of stays carrying a complication or major-complication code, expected from the principal-diagnosis chapter mix at all providers, above which the rate is material.
CLN-02-R03. Window before and after the claim in which the patient's other claims are read for a long-standing condition.
CLN-02-R03. Minimum number of the patient's claims in the look-back window before absence of a condition from history is used at all; the catalogue warns that absence is weak evidence.

CLN-02-R05. If mean length of stay or services per stay rise by at least this factor across the change point, the care changed as well and the severity rise is treated as corroborated (catalogue: without corresponding procedure, LOS or referral shift).
CLN-02-R05. A provider-month enters the case-severity series only with at least this many inpatient stays.
CLN-02-R05. The mean severity index after the change point must be at least this multiple of the level before it to be material.
CLN-03-R03. Window used when a care-pathway policy row does not state its own within_days for the required earlier step.
CLN-03-R02. A supporting diagnosis on any of the patient's claims within this many days before the service counts as an accepted indication (catalogue exclusion: lookback).
CLN-03-R04. Minimum service lines before a provider's rare-code share is compared with its specialty (catalogue exclusion: minimum volume).
CLN-03-R04, CLN-04-R05 and CLN-08-R05. Minimum number of comparable providers before a peer comparison is made at all; fewer peers cannot define what is usual.

CLN-03-R04. A service code is rare for a specialty when it makes up at most this share of the services billed by the OTHER providers of that specialty (leave-one-out, so a provider cannot make its own codes common).
CLN-03-R04. Minimum share of a provider's services that are rare for its specialty before it is reported for monitoring.
CLN-03-R04. The provider's rare-code share must also be at least this multiple of the median share of its specialty peers.
CLN-04-R05. Minimum referrals from a provider before its downstream spend per referral is compared with other referrers; a pattern that reliably triggers needs more than a handful.
CLN-04-R05. Besides a robust residual above robust_residual_flag_threshold, the mean downstream spend per referral must be at least this multiple of the peer median to be material.
CLN-04-R05. Claims by the same patient at the referral recipient within this many days of a referral are counted as its downstream services when the referral does not name the resulting claim.

CLN-04-R02 (line-level upgrade). A patient's service-day count must exceed this percentile of all patients using the same service family (and member_repeat_service_threshold) to be reported as excess frequency.

CLN-04-R02 (line-level upgrade). Trailing window in which a patient's service days in one service family are counted; an episode-length window rather than the half-year window used by the claim-header proxy.
CLN-04-R03. Two diagnostic services of the same code for the same patient this close together are a repeat whose justification depends on the first result.
CLN-04-R03. A first result recorded up to this many days after the repeat is treated as a reporting delay rather than an absent result (catalogue exclusion: result latency).
CLN-05-R04. Observed-to-expected admission ratio above which a hospital admits materially more of its comparable presentations than peers do.
CLN-05-R04. Minimum emergency presentations before a hospital's admission rate is compared with the rate expected from its diagnosis mix.

CLN-06-R01 and CLN-08-R03. A result or report is only expected once this many days have passed since the service, measured back from the latest service date in the file (catalogue exclusion: artefact latency).
CLN-06-R04. A member's denial given more than this many days after the service is not relied on (catalogue exclusion: recall).
CLN-06-R05. A condition must be billed on at least this many claims (across at least two months) before the absence of any medicine or result for it is examined.
CLN-06-R05. The absence of a footprint is only reported for conditions where at least this share of other patients with the same repeated condition do show medicine or results (versus peers).
CLN-06-R03 (line-level upgrade). Only claims with at least this many lines are compared, so that a single standard visit at the tariff price cannot look like a copied encounter.
CLN-06-R03 (line-level upgrade). Number of different patients at one provider that must share an identical line signature (codes, units, amounts and start times) before it is reported.

CLN-07-R01. Working minutes available to one clinician in a day (twelve hours); the capacity_tolerance_multiple margin is applied on top, so a breach means more than fifteen hours of minimum service time.
CLN-08-R05. Minimum laboratory tests before a provider's share of genetic or high-complexity tests is ranked against peers.
CLN-08-R05. The provider's shrunk rate of high-complexity tests must be at least this multiple of the peer mean, and its posterior interval must sit wholly above the peer mean.

CLN-08-R03. Only claims with at least this many numeric results are compared value-for-value across patients, so that a single common value (a normal template) cannot make two patients' results look copied.
CLN-08-R04. Minimum tests billed by a provider but performed by another laboratory before its mark-up is compared with other billing providers.
CLN-08-R04. Absolute floor on the median mark-up (billed price over the performing laboratory's own price), so that a modest handling margin is never reported however low the peer median.
CLN-08-R04. The provider's median mark-up over the performing laboratory's own price must be at least this multiple of the median mark-up of other pass-through billers.

CLN-01-R04 and CLN-02-R05. If the provider's mix of principal-diagnosis chapters moves by more than this total-variation distance across the change point, the patients changed and the shift is not treated as a coding change (catalogue: absent case-mix change; service-line expansion segmentation).
CLN-01-R04 and CLN-02-R05. Minimum number of monthly periods on EACH side of a candidate change point, so a before/after mean is never computed from one or two noisy months.
source: Chosen for this artefact; complements min_history_periods, which governs the total series length.

rationale: CLN-01-R04 and CLN-02-R05. Minimum standardised size of an upward before/after mean shift (pooled within-segment spread). Set high because the best of every admissible split is taken for every provider, which is a multiple-testing search.
source: Chosen for this artefact; calibrated so that month-to-month noise on the clean synthetic population does not declare a change.

rationale: CLN-01-R04 and CLN-02-R05. An ownership change or new contract within this many days of a detected change point is a known structural change and suppresses the signal (catalogue exclusion: segment known structural changes).
PAY-10-R01: number of insurers on the same event at or above which coordination of benefits must be evidenced.

CLN-01-R01. the control catalogue defines the trigger as a share that "exceeds shrunk PEER PERCENTILE", not a fixed rate, and this parameter is that percentile. An absolute rate would be wrong twice over: it would not adapt to a peer group's base rate, and on the claim extract the highest shrunk provider mismatch rate is 0.115, so any absolute cut above that would make the control unable to fire at all — which is a property of the number, not a finding about providers. At the 95th percentile the control raises roughly ten provider coding cases per run.
source: the control catalogue wording ('exceeds shrunk peer percentile'); the percentile is chosen for this artefact.

rationale: NET-02-R02, executing test. A community is abnormally dense when its internal edge density exceeds this multiple of the MEDIAN DENSITY OF COMMUNITIES OF THE SAME SIZE, pooled across all weekly snapshots. Size matching is required because density is a function of size in a bipartite graph.
source: the control catalogue exclusion column ('size matched communities'); the multiple is chosen for this artefact.

rationale: NET-02-R02, ABSOLUTE FLOOR only. Retained because the control catalogue describes an absolute density notion, but it is not the executing test: in a bipartite claims graph density falls roughly as 1/size, so an absolute cut flags every small community and no large one (at 0.35 it raises 686 signals from the weekly snapshots and breaches the alert-volume ceiling). The executing test is the SIZE-MATCHED comparison below, which is what the catalogue's own exclusion column — "specialty/geography/SIZE MATCHED communities" — actually asks for.
source: the control catalogue; retained as a reported floor, superseded by the size-matched test.

rationale: NET-02-R02 second condition: "LOW EXTERNAL FLOW". The share of a community's edges that leave the community must be below this for the community to be treated as closed. A dense community with high external flow is a hub, not a ring.
source: the control catalogue trigger wording; the value is chosen for this artefact.

rationale: NET-02-R02 third condition. "Member CIRCULATION" requires at least two members and at least two providers; a star of one provider and several members is a busy clinic, and flagging it would fill the queue with ordinary structure.
source: the control catalogue trigger wording ('member/provider edge density').

rationale: NET-02-R02: minimum Louvain community size before density statistics are computed, so that a two-node pair is not reported as a ring.
Per-feature weights of the transparent composite. Weights are published so a reviewer can reconstruct the score by hand from the per-feature contributions shown in the UI.

ANL-01-R01 transparent-composite score above which a provider lead is raised. This composite is the BENCHMARK every model must beat, so its threshold is set the way the design requires a threshold to be set — CALIBRATED TO REVIEWER CAPACITY, not to a fixed statistical significance level. At 1.2 the control raises roughly 17 provider leads per full run over 200 providers, which a four-reviewer team can absorb alongside the claim-level queue. The full score distribution (median 0.42, p95 1.44, max 2.21) is printed in validation_report.md so the position of this threshold within it is visible rather than asserted.
source: Calibrated to reviewer capacity to capacity; the score distribution it sits in is reported.

rationale: Tolerance applied to overlap detection to absorb same-day transfer and date-only (no time) records. Zero means any strict overlap counts.

CUSUM decision interval. Larger h means fewer false change points and slower detection. The conventional pairing with k=0.5 is h=4–5, which gives an in-control average run length of several hundred periods. Each provider in the claim extract has a MEDIAN OF 18 MONTHLY PERIODS, so an ARL that long makes detection arithmetically impossible rather than merely conservative: at h=5.0 the detector declares 0 change points across all 200 providers, which would be a property of the decision interval and not a finding about providers. h=3.0 is chosen so that the in-control ARL is commensurate with the series length actually available. This is a stated calibration to series length, NOT a threshold lowered until the control produced results — the observed volume at each candidate h is reported in validation_report.md so the choice is inspectable.
source: Page (1954) CUSUM, with the decision interval calibrated to the ~18-period series length in the claim extract.

rationale: CUSUM reference value (allowance), in standardised units — the shift size the chart is tuned to detect quickly (Page, 1954).
source: Standard CUSUM parameterisation for a 1-sigma shift.

rationale: ENT-02-R02 post-mortem service tolerance. NOT_EXECUTABLE on the claim extract (no death status).
DOC-01-R01. Days after submission within which a document the requirement policy names must arrive; a claim younger than this is not flagged, which is the catalogue's latency exclusion.
source: Chosen for this artefact; a payer would take it from its document-submission policy.

rationale: Longest searched passage quoted on a DOC-01-R03 or DOC-02-R04 signal. The quoted text and its offsets always match exactly; longer passages are cut at this length from their start so the evidence panel stays readable.
source: Chosen for this artefact (presentation of source spans, not a detection threshold).

rationale: DOC-02-R02. An age written in a note may differ from the registration age by a birthday or a rounding; only a difference larger than this is treated as the wrong patient's age.
DOC-02-R04. A note counts as generic when its patient-specific narrative (template lines removed) has fewer distinct words than this fraction of the peer median for the same note type and language.
DOC-02-R04. Share of a provider's high-complexity notes that must be generic before the provider is flagged; a single thin note is ordinary, a majority is a pattern.
DOC-02-R04. A provider needs at least this many notes for high-complexity services before the share of generic notes is judged; fewer is too small a denominator.
DOC-02-R01 cross-patient near-duplicate similarity threshold, computed after boilerplate removal.
Relative amount tolerance within which two claims are treated as the same billed service for PAY-01-R02 (5%).
Near-duplicate detection window for PAY-01-R02: same member, provider and diagnosis within this many days.

POL-01-R04. the control catalogue's trigger is a claim pattern that "exceeds tenure/risk-adjusted EXPECTATION", which is a comparison to the peer distribution rather than an extreme-tail cut. Only 29 claims in the claim extract fall inside the early-tenure window at all, so an extreme-tail threshold would reduce the control to noise. The 75th diagnosis-peer percentile means "above what three quarters of comparable claims cost", which is what "exceeds expectation" means in plain language.
source: the control catalogue wording; the percentile is chosen for this artefact.

rationale: A claim within this many days of policy inception is 'early tenure' (POL-01-R04, NET-04-R03). Early tenure is NEVER evidence of fraud on its own — the design says so explicitly and the control's disposition reflects that.
ENT-01-R01. Days after a cover period ends during which a service is still treated as covered, to absorb late posting of a renewal. A service further outside every cover period is flagged.
source: Chosen for this artefact; a payer would take this from its policy wording.

rationale: ENT-01-R04. How far back a referral to the treating provider may be dated and still satisfy a plan rule that the service needs a referral.

value: [["Abu Dhabi", "Dubai"], ["Dubai", "Sharjah"], ["Dubai", "Ajman"], ["Sharjah", "Ajman"], ["Sharjah", "Umm Al Quwain"], ["Ajman", "Umm Al Quwain"], ["Umm Al Quwain", "Ras Al Khaimah"], ["Sharjah", "Ras Al Khaimah"], ["Sharjah", "Fujairah"], ["Ras Al Khaimah", "Fujairah"]]
rationale: ENT-02-R04. Pairs of neighbouring emirates a member can plausibly visit on the same day; same-day use of one member's cover counts as a geographic observation only when the emirates are not neighbours.
source: Chosen for this artefact from UAE road geography; a payer would substitute travel times between its providers.

rationale: ENT-02-R04. Minimum number of independent observations (same-day use in two emirates, or a service that does not fit the member's age or sex) before a card-sharing pattern is raised, as the catalogue requires minimum independent evidence.
ENT-02-R02. Minimum reliability of the recorded death source for a post-mortem service to be flagged; a weaker source is left for data correction instead.
ENT-02-R01, POL-01-R01. A national-ID token shared by more member records than this is treated as a placeholder value rather than one person, and is excluded from identity-conflict checks.
ENT-03-R05. Minimum claims in the early window before a burst is assessed, so a provider with a handful of claims is never compared on a rate.
ENT-03-R05. A new or reactivated provider is flagged when its early monthly claim volume or value exceeds this percentile of established providers of the same facility type.
ENT-03-R05. A provider with no claims for at least this many days that then resumes billing is treated as reactivated after dormancy.
ENT-03-R01. Approved grace around a licence's start and end dates, covering renewals that the register records a few days late.
source: Chosen for this artefact; a regulator's renewal rules would set the real value.

rationale: ENT-03-R05. The early-activity window after a provider is credentialed, reactivated or resumes billing, over which its volume and value are compared with established peers.

ENT-03-R04 (cfg.specialty_map). The curated map of which treating-clinician specialties normally perform each code family. A code family not in the map is unconstrained; a clinician may also hold a cross-specialty privilege for the family.
source: Chosen for this artefact; a coding-policy owner would curate the real map.

rationale: ENT-04-R03 (cfg.max_concurrency). The most timed services one clinician may be billed for at the same moment before the day is flagged; two allows a brief handover overlap.
ENT-04-R04. Minimum minutes between the end of a clinician's service in one emirate and the start of the next in another emirate; a shorter gap is treated as an impossible journey.
source: Chosen for this artefact; a conservative inter-emirate drive time.

rationale: ENT-05-R02. Inpatient claims dated within this many days of the end of the file are not checked for admission evidence, because bed and discharge records can arrive late.
ENT-05-R04. Minimum claims on each side of the change point before a provider's setting mix is compared.
ENT-05-R04. Minimum rise in a provider's share of inpatient and day-case claims across its best change point before a setting shift is considered.
ENT-05-R04. Minimum months of history on each side of a candidate change point, so a single unusual month cannot be read as a shift.
ENT-05-R04. After the shift, the provider's inpatient share must also exceed this percentile of peer providers' shares, so a genuine hospital with a high share is not flagged.
ENT-06-R04. Minimum consultations a provider must have before its conversion rate into high-cost orders is compared with peers.
ENT-06-R04. The peer percentile of consultation-to-high-cost-order conversion rates a telehealth provider must exceed.
ENT-06-R04. A telehealth provider's conversion rate must be at least this multiple of the peer median, as well as above the peer percentile, to be flagged as materially exceeding peers.
ENT-06-R04. A downstream prescription, test or device order at or above this amount (or a product the drug policy marks high-cost) counts as a high-cost conversion of a consultation.
ENT-06-R02. A telehealth consultation shorter than this that nevertheless produces an order is treated as lacking a meaningful clinical interaction.
source: Chosen for this artefact; matches the shortest telephone evaluation code (5-10 minutes).

rationale: ENT-06-R03. If fewer suppliers of the same type than this operate in the supplier's emirate, concentration is explained by a narrow network and is not flagged.
ENT-06-R02. The missing-note limb applies only to providers whose other teleconsults carry a note at least this often, so absent documentation is meaningful rather than a gap in what the file holds.
ENT-06-R02, ENT-06-R04. Days after a consultation within which a prescription or referral by the same clinician for the same patient is attributed to that consultation.
ENT-06-R03. Minimum downstream orders (prescriptions and referrals) a provider must have before its concentration on one supplier is measured.
ENT-06-R03. A telehealth provider's top-supplier share must exceed this percentile of other prescribing providers' top-supplier shares, as well as the governed referral_concentration_threshold.
ENT-06-R03, ENT-06-R04. A provider is treated as a telehealth provider when at least this share of its visits are remote.

ENT-01-R01, ENT-02-R01, POL-01-R01. A baby younger than this is treated as covered under, and identified through, a parent's policy, so missing cover, a shared ID or an absent roster entry is not flagged.
source: Chosen for this artefact; reflects the common 30-day newborn cover convention in UAE plans.

rationale: DELIBERATELY UNREACHABLE (>1.0). The design prohibits automatic merging of low-confidence matches; this artefact never auto-merges at all. Every candidate is surfaced for human confirmation.
Minimum match confidence for a candidate pair to be SURFACED to a human reviewer. Below this it is noise.
EWMA control-limit width in sigma units.
EWMA smoothing constant for monthly normalised provider metrics.
PAY-01-R01 is a HARD edit and may REJECT. It therefore requires exact amount equality — no tolerance, no statistical judgement. This is the safety boundary expressed as a number.
Fully loaded reviewer cost per case, used for the 'net savings after review cost' metric. Without it, net savings cannot be computed and would be reported as NOT_MEASURABLE.
source: Chosen for this artefact; a real deployment would take this from payroll and overhead allocation.

rationale: Hard-edit gate: ≥99% decision reproducibility. Quoted as an acceptance criterion.
Data-readiness gate: ≥99.5% key linkage for claims and lines. Quoted from the specification as an acceptance criterion, NOT as a result.
Statistical-rule gate: review yield above an agreed baseline after a prospective shadow period.
source: Chosen for this artefact; the design requires a baseline, not a number.

rationale: Graph edges are materialised into WEEKLY, time-bounded snapshots. An edge exists only within its snapshot window.
Nominal contamination used only to initialise the score; the OPERATIONAL threshold is set by reviewer capacity, not by this value.
Isolation Forest ensemble size (Liu et al., 2008).
Maximum expected latency per execution stage, reproduced from the design specification. Measured per stage during the validation run and reported against the ceiling.
Local Outlier Factor neighbourhood size (Breunig et al., 2000). LOF is retained because it surfaces anomalies that are only anomalous relative to a local peer cluster.
CLN-05-R01: robust residual of length of stay against the diagnosis-peer distribution, above/below which utilisation review is raised.
ENT-02-R03: a member cannot be an inpatient in two places at once. Overlapping admissions for one member are an impossible-presence lead.
source: Physical impossibility; the tolerance, not the principle, is configurable.

rationale: Normaliser for independent_domain_count (rule / statistical / network / document / model).
source: Derived from the five detection domains.

rationale: ENT-02-R03 travel-speed impossibility limit. NOT_EXECUTABLE on the claim extract (no geography) and classified as such in the coverage matrix.
Entities whose empirical-Bayes posterior interval is wider than this are EXCLUDED FROM RANKING rather than flagged on a falsely precise point estimate (an explicit design requirement).
source: The peer design requires the mechanism; the numeric width is chosen for this artefact.

rationale: PAY-08-R03: attempts per underlying service above which a resubmission-loop provider case is raised.
CLN-04-R02: admissions per member within the velocity window above which episode-frequency excess is raised.
Minimum claim count for an entity before any peer-relative rate is computed at all. Below this the entity is reported as insufficient evidence, not as a low-rate entity.
Minimum number of monthly periods of provider history before a CUSUM/EWMA change point may be DECLARED (explicit requirement).
source: The change-detection design requires a configured minimum; the value is chosen for this artefact.

rationale: Minimum number of entities in a peer group before it may be used; below this the hierarchy backs off to the parent level and records peer_level_used.
CLN-04-R01: same/equivalent service repeated inside this interval without an accepted indicator.
Maximum expected calibration error permitted at the model promotion gate.

Minimum PROSPECTIVE lift in review yield over the ANL-01-R01 transparent composite, on a strictly later period, before a model may move from shadow to active. If the model does not clear this, the honest verdict is printed and the model stays in shadow.
source: The design specification the promotion gate requires demonstrated prospective lift; the 1.10 factor is chosen for this artefact.

rationale: Fraction of the claim-date-ordered timeline used for model TRAINING. The split is strictly temporal — training data is always earlier than scoring data.
NET-01-R02. Each direction must also be a material part of the referrer's own referrals, so a large provider's handful of referrals to a partner is not treated as a loop.

NET-01-R02. Each direction's share of the referrer's referrals must be at least this multiple of what the recipient's share of all referrals predicts, so a popular hospital receiving many referrals is not a loop.

NET-01-R02. Each direction of a referral loop must carry at least this many referrals; below it a two-way flow is within the ordinary exchange of transfers between neighbouring hospitals and too thin to call a loop.
NET-01-R03. When a referral does not name the claim it resulted in, the member's first claim at the recipient within this many days is taken as its result.
NET-01-R03. A referral converts to a high-cost service when its resulting claim carries a line at or above this percentile of all positive line values in the file.
NET-01-R03. Poisson tail probability of seeing at least the observed conversions given the expected number; the excess must also be unlikely by chance, not only large in ratio.
NET-01-R03. Observed high-cost conversions must be at least this multiple of the number expected for the same recipient specialty and referral reason (case-mix adjustment).
NET-01-R03. Minimum referrals received before a recipient's conversion rate is compared with expectation; fewer gives a rate too noisy to rank.
NET-01-R04. A referrer needs at least this many laboratory, imaging or pharmacy referrals before the share kept inside linked providers is judged.
NET-01-R04. Share of a referrer's downstream referrals that must go to providers covertly linked to it (shared bank, phone or address, different declared owner) for the chain to be called closed.

NET-02-R01 and NET-04-R04. An identifier shared by more providers than this is treated as a shared service (a billing bureau, a building) rather than a covert link, which is the catalogue's shared-services exclusion.
NET-02-R04. A provider has become central when its average monthly rank by distinct members served is at or above this percentile in the window from the change on.

NET-02-R04. The catalogue asks for MATERIAL exposure: the provider must bill at least this much in the window after the change for the rise to be worth a network review (for a clinic, several months of outpatient billing).
NET-02-R04. A provider is peripheral when its average monthly rank by distinct members served is at or below this percentile in the window before the change.
NET-02-R04. Months averaged before and after a candidate change month; averaging over several months stops one busy month from looking like a structural change.

NET-03-R01 on a multi-table file. The benefit-exhaustion limb is met when the member has used at least this share of the yearly benefit limit for the pair's benefit family; it raises confidence and is reported, not required.

NET-03-R01 on a multi-table file. A patient-provider pair must exceed this percentile of pairs at the same provider type and benefit family on BOTH number of claims and total value; comparing like with like is what stops a patient's ordinary refills or follow-ups from looking like a suspicious pair.
NET-03-R02. The 'same few providers' a closed group uses: the group's claims are measured at this many of its most-used providers.
NET-03-R02. Share of the employer group's claims that must stay with those few providers for the group to be called closed.

NET-03-R02. Share of a provider's distinct patients that must come from one employer or sponsor for the activity to be called concentrated; it acts together with the catchment-adjusted lift and the closure share, which carry most of the discrimination.
NET-03-R02. That employer's share of the provider's patients must be at least this multiple of its share of members in the provider's emirate, which is the clinic-catchment adjustment.
NET-03-R02. A provider must serve at least this many distinct members before the employer mix of its patients is judged.
NET-03-R03. A claim is high-value when one of its lines is at or above this percentile of all positive line values in the file.
NET-03-R03. A provider needs at least this many claims before its zero-patient-share and repeated high-value rates are compared with all providers.
NET-03-R03. Distinct patients who must show both a zero patient share and repeated high-value services at the provider, so the signature is a group pattern rather than one patient.
NET-03-R03. Both inducement limbs (zero patient share, repeated high-value services) must be at least this multiple of the pooled rate across all providers; either alone is common.
NET-03-R04. Distinct patients whose authenticated confirmations or complaints must corroborate each other before a provider is escalated; one account alone is handled as a single complaint.
Minimum OCR-adjusted extraction confidence for a DOC/CLN-01-R03 finding to be rendered. A finding with NO SOURCE SPAN is discarded entirely regardless of confidence (non-negotiable).

Share of generated SYNTHETIC discharge summaries deliberately made inconsistent with their claim, so the document pipeline has both positive and negative cases. Every such document is marked SYNTHETIC in its filename and body.

ANL-01-R04: minimum HDBSCAN cluster size before a residual-space cluster is proposed as a candidate typology for the quarterly review. Disposition is MONITOR_ONLY only. The value is bounded by the population that is actually scored: entity isolation leaves 95 providers in the scoring set, so a minimum of 15 would require a single typology to cover 16% of all scored providers and produces zero clusters. Eight is roughly 8% of the scored population — small enough to surface a pattern, large enough that a cluster is not three providers and a coincidence.
source: Chosen for this artefact, bounded by the entity-isolated scoring population.

rationale: PAY-01-R04: amount by which the combined payments of two insurers may exceed the billed amount before a coordinated payment is treated as a cross-payer duplicate. It absorbs rounding in the two insurers' patient-share arithmetic, nothing more.
source: Chosen for this artefact; one dirham of rounding across two remittances.

rationale: PAY-02-R02: days either side of a parent procedure within which an included component billed on a different claim for the same patient is treated as part of the same service. Kept short so that genuinely separate later care is not swept in; a longer global surgical period would be a contract-specific setting.
source: Chosen for this artefact; same-day or next-day billing of a bundled component.

rationale: PAY-02-R05 minimum volume: a provider must bill the code pair together on at least this many claims before its co-occurrence rate is compared with peers. Below it the rate is too thin to justify a policy review.
source: Chosen for this artefact; the catalogue names a minimum volume without a value.

rationale: PAY-02-R05 and PAY-05-R03 peer adjustment: minimum number of other providers in the same type and specialty needed before a provider is compared with them. With fewer the peer rate is not a population rate.
source: Chosen for this artefact; consistent with the three-entity minimum of the Beta prior fit.

rationale: PAY-02-R05: floor on the provider's shrunk co-billing rate. A pair billed together on a small share of claims is not a billing habit even when peers almost never bill it, so this keeps rare-pair ratios out of the policy-review queue.

PAY-02-R05: a provider's shrunk co-billing rate for a code pair must be at least this multiple of its peers' rate. Shrinkage already pulls small providers toward the peer rate, so the multiple describes a genuine behavioural difference, not noise.

PAY-02-R03: the package definition lists every activity a package may include without marking which are indispensable, so a component counts as a core (required) activity when it appears on at least this share of the claims for that package. Nine in ten keeps optional tests and alternative visit levels out of the core.
source: Chosen for this artefact; a stand-in for a mandatory-activity list the file does not carry.

rationale: PAY-02-R03: a package needs at least this many claims in the file before its core activities are inferred from them; with fewer, the missing-activity limb is not run for that package.

PAY-02-R03: share of a package's core activities that must be absent from the claim before the package is reported as incomplete. A missing listing or two is usually a reporting slip or a different visit level; three quarters or more missing means the package was billed without its core activities.

PAY-02-R02 exclusion: indicators that mark a line as the professional or the technical part of a split service. A component carrying one of them is the contractual professional/facility split the catalogue excludes, not a duplicate of the parent.
source: Chosen for this artefact; conventional professional (26) and technical (TC) component indicators.

rationale: PAY-02-R03 and PAY-02-R04: a package component that must be listed at zero price counts as charged, or as paid separately, only above this amount. It exists so that a fils of rounding is not reported as a charge.

PAY-03-R04 rounding policy: billed time-based minutes may exceed the recorded service window by up to this many minutes, and two timed services by one clinician may overlap by up to this many, before either is reported. Seven minutes mirrors the usual rule that a unit needs at least eight minutes of service.
source: Chosen for this artefact; mirrors the conventional eight-minute rule for timed units.

rationale: PAY-03-R03 exclusion: bilateral, laterality and repeat-procedure indicators. A group of lines carrying one of them may legitimately exceed the single-side daily maximum, so it is not reported.
source: Chosen for this artefact; conventional bilateral (50), side (RT/LT) and repeat (76/77) indicators.

rationale: PAY-04-R05 exclusion switch: whether policy permits one approval to be shared by family members under the same sponsor. The catalogue allows shared approvals only where policy permits; no such policy exists for this artefact, so sharing is not permitted.
source: Chosen for this artefact; the catalogue's 'family/shared authorization only if policy permits'.

rationale: PAY-04-R02 urgent retrospective route: an emergency service delivered up to this many days before its approval started is treated as approved after the event rather than as outside the approval's dates.
PAY-04-R04: amount by which the cumulative billed value may exceed an approval's approved value before the excess is reported, absorbing rounding across several claims.
PAY-05-R02 document-arrival latency: a claim submitted fewer than this many days before the file's last submission is not judged, because its supporting report may still be on its way.
PAY-05-R04 exclusion: days after an edit takes effect that are ignored as the rule-launch and provider-education period, so that transitional billing is not read as migration.
PAY-05-R04 minimum volume: a provider must bill the edited procedure on at least this many claims after the education period before a change in its behaviour is assessed.

PAY-05-R04: rise, in share of the provider's claims with the edited procedure, of paid lines that escape the edit (by a modifier or an unedited code) between before and after the edit. Thirty points is a behavioural change, not drift.
PAY-05-R04: length of the comparison windows before and after a bundling edit takes effect, over which a provider's rate of escaping the edit is measured.
source: Chosen for this artefact; four months either side gives enough claims per provider.

rationale: PAY-05-R03: the shrunk modifier use rate must also exceed the peer mean by at least this many percentage points (as a fraction). When peers almost never use a modifier, a multiple of their tiny rate is met by two or three uses; the absolute gap keeps such providers out of the audit queue.
PAY-05-R03 minimum denominator: a provider needs at least this many service lines before its modifier use rate is ranked against peers; the larger of this and min_entity_opportunities applies.
source: Chosen for this artefact; the catalogue names a minimum denominator without a value.

rationale: PAY-05-R03: a provider's shrunk modifier use rate must lie above this percentile of the use rates of its peers (the other providers of the same type and specialty, leaving the provider itself out), as the catalogue's 'exceeds shrunk specialty peer percentile' requires.
source: The catalogue wording; the percentile is chosen for this artefact.

rationale: PAY-05-R03: the shrunk rate must also be at least this multiple of the peer mean. A percentile alone always selects the top few providers even in a population with no abnormal behaviour; the multiple keeps the control silent on such a population.

PAY-05-R02: indicators that unlock extra payment only with a supporting operative report or note (increased procedural service, co-surgeon, surgical team). A line carrying one with no Observation and no claim document is pended.
source: Chosen for this artefact; conventional documentation-dependent indicators.

rationale: PAY-06-R01 absolute rounding tolerance, added to the percentage tolerance, so that sub-dirham differences on low-priced codes are not repriced.
PAY-06-R01 rounding tolerance: a submitted unit price may exceed the contracted allowed price by this fraction before the line is repriced, absorbing rounding of discounts and unit conversions.
PAY-07-R04: receipted member payments may exceed the approved patient share by at most this many dirhams (rounding, card fees) before a balance-billing case is raised.
PAY-07-R04 exclusion: receipt lines describing a non-covered elective item bought with documented consent are not counted against the patient share.
PAY-07-R02: the amount claimed from the insurer may exceed billed less discount less patient share by at most this many dirhams (rounding) before the claim is repriced.

value: ["overcharg", "balance bill", "charged more", "extra payment", "asked to pay more", "paid more than"]
rationale: PAY-07-R04: a member complaint whose type or text contains any of these is treated as an overcharge complaint about the linked claim.
PAY-07-R03: a patient share below the benefit calculation that is an exact multiple of this unit counts as a rounded-down share, alongside zero shares.
source: Chosen for this artefact; whole tens of dirhams are the common manual rounding.

rationale: PAY-07 rounding exclusion: a patient share within this many dirhams of the benefit calculation is treated as rounding, not as a mismatch. Also the floor below which a share counts as zero for PAY-07-R03.
source: Chosen for this artefact; covers fils-level rounding across several lines.

rationale: PAY-07 exemptions exclusion: a benefit rule whose exceptions text contains any of these terms is treated as an exemption and its claims are not compared with the co-payment percentage.
source: Chosen for this artefact; a real deployment would read a structured exemption flag.

rationale: PAY-07-R01 relative rounding tolerance: the larger of this share of the expected patient share and the absolute tolerance must be exceeded before a mismatch is raised.
PAY-07-R03: a provider needs at least this many claims on which the plan expects a patient share before its zero-share rate is compared with peers; fewer is insufficient evidence.

PAY-07-R03: the shrunk rate must also exceed the product-adjusted peer rate by at least this absolute margin, so a provider with one waived share out of a hundred is never raised however low the peer rate is.
PAY-07-R03 regulator-programme exclusion: products whose name contains any of these carry a zero or regulated share by design and are left out of the zero-share comparison.
source: Chosen for this artefact; UAE programmes with zero or fixed co-payment.

rationale: PAY-07-R03: the provider's shrunk zero-or-rounded share rate must be at least this multiple of the product-adjusted peer rate to be raised.

PAY-08-R02 accepted-correction matrix: for a refusal whose code starts with the key, changing the listed fields is an expected correction and is not pended. Refusals for medical necessity or non-coverage accept no reimbursement-field change.
source: Chosen for this artefact; a payer would maintain this per denial code.

rationale: PAY-08-R03 exclusion: attempts whose resubmission type names the internal complaint or appeal route are not counted towards the attempt limit.
PAY-08-R04: at least this share of the provider's successful changed resubmissions must follow one refusal reason, which is what 'concentrates on specific denial edits' means here.
PAY-08-R01 exclusion: resubmissions whose type names a permitted legacy route are not checked for a prior-claim reference.
PAY-08-R03: resubmissions of one underlying service beyond this number (formal appeals excluded) are raised as a resubmission loop.
PAY-08: a changed field whose name contains any of these is reimbursement-enabling (diagnosis, code, units, provider, setting or indicator, as the catalogue lists).
source: Control catalogue PAY-08-R02 trigger; tokens chosen for this artefact.

rationale: PAY-08-R04: a provider needs at least this many changed resubmissions after a refusal before its success rate is compared with other providers.
PAY-08-R04: the provider's shrunk success rate on changed resubmissions must exceed other providers' rate by at least this absolute margin, which is what 'materially exceeds peers' means here.
PAY-08-R03: a chain with at least this many resubmissions, each changing a different set of fields, that ends in payment is raised as trying variants until paid.

PAY-09-R03: visit settings in which the disguise-risk combinations apply (elective cosmetic work is done as an outpatient or day case); an inpatient stay is left out. Applied only when the visit setting is recorded.

PAY-09-R04: words ignored when comparing a receipt description with billed services, because they describe the payment or its broad category (consultation, medicines, laboratory, imaging, admission) rather than the item.
PAY-09-R01 NLP-confidence exclusion: documents read with OCR confidence below this are not used to raise a conflict.
PAY-09-R01 NLP-confidence exclusion: a non-covered term preceded within the negation window by any of these (for example 'not cosmetic') is not treated as describing the service.
source: Chosen for this artefact; a simple negation window in the NegEx tradition.

rationale: PAY-09-R01: number of characters before a matched term that are searched for a negation word.

value: ["cosmetic", "aesthetic", "botox", "botulinum toxin for wrinkles", "dermal filler", "hair transplant", "teeth whitening", "liposuction", "weight loss programme", "slimming", "anti-ageing", "anti-aging", "tattoo removal", "\u062a\u062c\u0645\u064a\u0644", "\u062a\u062c\u0645\u064a\u0644\u064a"]
rationale: PAY-09-R01: phrases in an attached note that describe a service the standard UAE benefit excludes. Supplemented at run time by the excluded-service names in the disguise-risk policy table when the file carries one.
source: Chosen for this artefact from common UAE plan exclusions; Arabic terms for cosmetic included.

rationale: PAY-09-R04: a member receipt whose description shares less than this word overlap (Jaccard) with every billed service description is treated as describing a different item.
PAY-09-R03 reconstructive exclusion: a claim carrying any of these diagnoses (cancer, reconstruction aftercare, burns, cleft lip and palate, facial trauma) is treated as reconstructive, not cosmetic.
source: Chosen for this artefact from ICD-10-CM chapters for reconstructive indications.

rationale: PAY-09-R02: a provider needs at least this many refused services followed by a substitute before it is compared with peers.
PAY-09-R02: the provider's shrunk substitution rate must exceed other providers' rate by at least this absolute margin, which is what 'unusually often' means here.
PAY-09-R02: a paid, different code billed for the same patient at the same provider within this many days after a refused service counts as a possible substitution.
PAY-09-R04 confirmation-reliability exclusion: confirmations received through these channels lower the signal's confidence rather than being taken at face value.
PAY-10-R03: ICD-10 external-cause codes that point to a road-traffic (V01-V99) or work-related (Y96, Y99.0) event, where another party may be liable.
source: ICD-10-CM external-cause chapter; selection chosen for this artefact.

rationale: PAY-10-R03 clinical false-positive list: external-cause codes that look like accidents but rarely involve a liable third party (leisure, unspecified status, own roller-skate or skateboard falls).
PAY-10-R02: all payers' payments plus the patient share may exceed the allowed charge by at most this many dirhams (rounding) before an overpayment is raised.
PAY-10-R04: a payment made after a third-party settlement may exceed the amount still due after the settlement is deducted by at most this many dirhams.
PAY-11-R01: roles authorised to override a refusal or failed payment check. An override by any other role is raised.
source: Chosen for this artefact; a payer's delegated-authority matrix would replace it.

rationale: PAY-11-R02: an adjudicator needs at least this many overrides on one provider's claims before the pair is compared with colleagues.

PAY-11-R02: the adjudicator's override rate on the provider must be at least this multiple of the colleague rate on the same provider, the adjudicator's own rate elsewhere and the overall rate, which is what 'materially exceeds adjusted peers' means here.
PAY-11: a system edit result containing any of these means the automated check did not pass, so a manual approval afterwards is an override.

PAY-11-R04: edit results that mark a claim as flagged by a payment check or pended for manual review, so that full-payment rates are compared only on comparable, flagged claims. Explicit overrides are left to PAY-11-R01 and PAY-11-R02.
PAY-11-R04: the standard deviation of paid-to-requested ratios for the pair must be at most this (low variance), so a pair that pays in full but also trims some claims is not raised.
PAY-11-R04: an adjudicator and provider pair needs at least this many decisions on flagged claims before its full-payment rate is compared.
PAY-11-R04: the pair's full-payment rate on flagged claims must exceed the rate elsewhere by at least this absolute margin, which is what 'unusually high approval' means here.
PAY-11-R04: a decision paying at least one minus this fraction of the requested amount counts as payment in full.
PAY-11-R01 exclusions: an override whose recorded reason names emergency escalation or delegated authority is not raised.
PAY-11-R03: upward adjustments after settlement smaller than this many dirhams (rounding corrections) are not raised.
PAY-11-R03 exclusions: an upward adjustment is justified when an adjudication event or claim version for the claim names an appeal decision or a contract true-up.

PAY-12-R01 timing and netting exclusion: a cancelled claim whose payment has not yet been reversed is raised only once this many days have passed since the cancellation, allowing for netting in the next payment run.
source: Chosen for this artefact; roughly one monthly payment cycle.

rationale: PAY-12: payments within this many dirhams of the payable amount are treated as rounding; used for duplicate payments, residual payments on cancelled claims and credits exceeding what was paid.
PAY-12-R04: a provider needs at least this many credits taken against unrelated claims, or claims with negative lines, before the limb is compared with peers.
PAY-12-R04: the provider's rate of unrelated offsets or negative-line claims must be at least this multiple of the peer rate (repeated, versus peers).
PAY-12-R03: a provider refund or credit must be linked to the recovery it settles within this many days of receipt.
source: Chosen for this artefact; a payer's finance SLA would replace it.

rationale: PAY-12-R03 exclusions: a credit whose status or note names a dispute or the unapplied-cash queue is not raised.
PAY-12-R04: a provider whose median days from cancellation to reversal is at least this multiple of the peer median is raised as delaying reversals.
PHR-03-R03: pharmacy bill share exceeding this multiple of the diagnosis-peer median is a spike candidate.

value: ["perfume", "fragrance", "cosmetic", "skincare", "skin care", "shampoo", "sunscreen", "makeup", "make-up", "baby formula", "infant formula", "protein powder", "slimming", "hair dye", "toiletries", "electronics", "mobile phone", "gift card", "voucher", "sunglasses", "diapers", "nappies", "chocolate", "energy drink"]
rationale: PHR-01-R04: words on a member's receipt that name a non-medical or uncovered item. A receipt naming one of these against a claim that billed a covered medicine is the substitution evidence the catalogue describes.
source: Chosen for this artefact; a governed term list the special investigations unit maintains.

rationale: PHR-01-R02/R03: billed quantity or strength may exceed the prescribed, approved or dispensed figure by this fraction before it is a finding, which absorbs pack-size conversion and rounding to whole packs.
source: Chosen for this artefact; a whole-pack rounding allowance, not a regulatory figure.

rationale: PHR-01-R04: confidence given to a receipt-only substitution finding. It rises part of the way towards one when the pharmacy's stock record also could not cover the billed medicine that month.
source: Chosen for this artefact; receipts are member-supplied and not independently verified.

rationale: PHR-01-R04 confirmation reliability: a receipt is only tied to a dispensing record when it is dated within this many days of the fill; a receipt further away may be for another visit.

PHR-01-R03 stock limb: a pharmacy's billed quantity for one product in one month may exceed opening stock plus purchases by this fraction before it is flagged, because deliveries posted a few days late shift stock between months.
source: Chosen for this artefact; covers the claim-timing differences the catalogue names as an exclusion.

rationale: PHR-02-R01/R04: days of earlier supply a member may still hold when refilling the same or an equivalent medicine. Beyond this the refill is early; a week covers routine refill-reminder behaviour and weekends.
source: Chosen for this artefact; payers commonly allow a refill once most of a 30-day supply is used.

rationale: PHR-02-R01: the allowed overlap at a refill is the larger of the fixed overlap days and this fraction of the previous fill's days' supply, so a medicine given every eight weeks earns a proportionate refill window (refill once 80% of the supply is used).
source: Chosen for this artefact; mirrors the common 80%-used refill rule.

rationale: PHR-02-R02 chronic-therapy exclusion: therapeutic classes used as long-term maintenance treatment. Their course limits are review points handled by approvals, so continuous fills of these classes are not flagged as exceeding a treatment duration.
source: Chosen for this artefact; the classes follow the drug policy's therapeutic_class vocabulary.

rationale: PHR-02-R02: fills of one medicine are one continuous course while each new fill arrives within this many days of the previous supply running out; a longer gap starts a new course.
PHR-02-R01 inpatient exclusion: a refill within this many days after an inpatient discharge is discharge medication and is not treated as an early refill.
PHR-02-R02: a course on one prescription may run this fraction beyond the drug policy's maximum duration before it is flagged, which absorbs refill timing and pack rounding at the end of a course.
PHR-02-R04: number of different pharmacies supplying overlapping courses of one equivalent medicine to a member at which the member is flagged. Two alone is often a stock shortage or partial fill.

PHR-02-R03: number of unrelated prescribing units (different facilities with different declared owners) of one equivalent medicine within the window at which a member is flagged. Two covers a referral or second opinion.
PHR-02-R03: the same threshold for controlled medicines, kept as a separate governed value so a policy owner can lower it for controlled drugs without changing the general threshold.
PHR-02-R03: the window in which distinct prescribers of one equivalent medicine are counted for a member; ninety days spans three monthly refills.
PHR-03-R01: a daily dose may exceed the drug policy's mg/kg/day limit by this fraction before it is flagged, which absorbs tablet-strength rounding and a recorded weight that is a few months old.

PHR-03-R02: diagnoses recorded for the member on any claim within this many days before a fill count as the indication for that medicine, so a chronic condition coded last quarter still supports this month's refill.
PHR-03-R01 loading-dose exclusion: a member's first fill of a medicine lasting this many days or fewer may legitimately carry a higher loading dose.

PHR-03-R02 rare-disease exclusion: members with a diagnosis in these ICD-10 blocks (inborn metabolic disorders, cystic fibrosis, haemophilias, primary immunodeficiencies, motor neurone and muscular disorders) are not flagged for indication or step-therapy gaps.
source: Chosen for this artefact; a representative subset of ICD-10 rare-disease blocks.

rationale: PHR-03-R04: when peers bill no wastage beyond the vial arithmetic at all, a provider must average at least this many whole vials of excess per line to be flagged, so rounding noise never fires.
PHR-03-R04: a provider needs at least this many lines of one vial drug before its wastage is compared, so one unusual administration is never a pattern.
PHR-03-R04: a drug needs at least this many providers billing it before any of them is compared with the others.
PHR-03-R04: a provider is flagged when its average billed wastage above the vial arithmetic, per line, is at least this multiple of the median of other providers giving the same drug.
PHR-04-R03 product-availability exclusion: if every high-cost product involved is stocked by fewer than this many pharmacies, concentration reflects availability rather than steering.
PHR-04-R04: a new link is dominant when it takes at least this share of the prescriber's prescriptions within the ramp months.
PHR-04-R03: both the high-cost and the other prescriptions of a prescriber must number at least this many before their concentrations are compared.

PHR-04-R03: a prescriber is flagged when the share of their high-cost prescriptions going to one pharmacy exceeds the share of their other prescriptions going there by at least this many share points.

PHR-04-R02: a clinic-to-pharmacy flow is concentrated when at least this share of the clinic's prescriptions go to that pharmacy; it is a finding only when the two also share a bank account, phone or address.
PHR-04-R01: the minimum number of peer prescribers for a peer comparison; with fewer the comparison falls back to a broader peer group.
PHR-04-R01/R02: a prescriber (or clinic) needs at least this many dispensed prescriptions before its pharmacy concentration is assessed; below it one pharmacy can dominate by chance.
PHR-04-R01 narrow-network exclusion: where fewer than this many pharmacies dispense in the prescriber's emirate, concentration reflects access rather than steering.

PHR-04-R04: the prescriber must have prescribed in at least this many months before the link first appears, so the link is new against an established practice, and the pharmacy itself must have been dispensing that long (new-site exclusion).
PHR-04-R01: how far, in share points, a prescriber's top-pharmacy share must exceed the median of prescribers of the same specialty and emirate.
PHR-04-R04: the new link must carry at least this many prescriptions in the ramp months, so a low-volume prescriber switching once is not a pattern.
PHR-04-R04: the number of months, starting with a new prescriber-pharmacy link's first month, over which its share of the prescriber's prescriptions is measured.
PHR-04-R01: the share of a prescriber's prescriptions filled at one pharmacy at or above which the concentration can be a finding; it must also exceed peers by the margin.
PHR-05-R03 member-growth exclusion: members younger than this age at re-issue are not flagged on the useful-life limb, because growing children outgrow devices before their useful life.
PHR-05-R01: when a rented device is billed as a purchase, the line is repriced to this fraction of the billed purchase price as the payable rental charge.
source: Chosen for this artefact; stands in for the contract's monthly rental rate.

rationale: PHR-05-R02 replacement exclusion: an implant billed without a same-day procedure is not flagged when the member had a qualifying procedure within this many days before (a staged or replacement implant).
PHR-05-R03: an item needs at least this many billed lines before its median quantity is used as the norm.
PHR-05-R03: supply units on a line at or above this multiple of the median units billed for the same item are flagged as beyond the usual consumption.
PHR-05-R01: when a used device is billed as new, the line is repriced to this fraction of the billed new price.
source: Chosen for this artefact; stands in for the contract's used-equipment rate.

rationale: PHR-05-R03 useful-life limb: a device re-issued to the same member before this fraction of the previous device's expected useful life has passed is flagged.

PHR-01-R02 titration and PHR-02-R01 dose-change exclusions: a daily dose that differs from the member's previous fill of the same medicine by more than this fraction is a dose change, which legitimately explains a new strength or an early refill.
POL-01-R05. At least this share of the cohort's early claims must go to one group of providers that share an owner, bank account, phone or address before the cluster is raised.
POL-01-R05. Minimum cohort size before an employer's or broker's early-claim rate is compared with other cohorts (the portfolio-size exclusion).
POL-01-R05. The cohort's early-claim rate must exceed this percentile of other employers' or brokers' cohorts.
POL-01-R05. Members added by one employer or broker within one window of this many days are assessed together as an enrolment cohort.
POL-01-R03. Application declarations are compared with prior history only within this many days of the application, standing in for the contestability period in which the law allows the comparison.
source: Chosen for this artefact; a legal owner would set the real period.

rationale: POL-01-R02. A service counts as high-cost when its gross amount is at or above this quantile of all claims in the file.
POL-01-R03. Prior cover ending more than this many days before the application is not treated as material to the declaration.
POL-01-R02. An add or change may be backdated by up to this many days (the enrolment SLA); a longer backdating over a high-cost service is flagged unless it is an approved retroactive correction.
Credible-interval mass reported beside every shrunk rate.
Divisor inside log1p(exposure_aed / 1000) in the priority formula.
source: Design specification for the priority formula.

rationale: Reproduced EXACTLY from the design specification. These are not tunable in this artefact without a recorded governance change, because the formula's auditability is the point: the UI renders each term's contribution.
source: Design specification for the priority formula.

rationale: CLN-07-R02: conservative plausible concurrent-admission capacity per provider per day before throughput impossibility is raised. Deliberately generous so the control flags impossibility, not busyness.
source: Chosen for this artefact. A real deployment would take licensed bed counts from the regulator file.

rationale: PSI above which drift is BREACHED and recalibration or kill switch is recommended.
Population Stability Index above which drift is WARNED.
Stratified random-audit sample size. The random audit is the only mechanism capable of estimating a false-negative rate.
source: Chosen for this artefact; gives roughly ±4pp precision on a proportion at 95% confidence.

rationale: Fixed seed so that `python -m fwa.run_validation` is deterministic and every reported figure is reproducible (the Definition of Done).
Readmission window for CLN-05-R02/R03. A related admission inside this window with payment impact triggers episode review — explicitly 'not a fraud label' (control catalogue, CLN-05-R02).
source: Chosen for this artefact; 30 days is the common industry readmission window.

rationale: Half-life used to normalise the `recency` term of the priority formula into [0,1].
source: Chosen for this artefact; the design specifies the term, not its shape.

rationale: NET-01-R01 and NET-04-R02. the control catalogue compares top-recipient share to PEERS, and on the claim extract the highest agent top-provider share is 0.037 because 20 agents spread across 200 providers — so the absolute threshold below (cfg.referral_concentration_threshold) is never met and is reported as not met rather than quietly lowered.
